messages.principle: N = not h is the only NOT, so h is NOT-free/monotone. Every wire g equals C0_g on {h=1} and C1_g on {h=0} (C0/C1 = NOT replaced by const 0/1, both monotone, C0 <= C1). So g is monotone along any chain inside {h=1} and inside {h=0}.
messages.P_scheme: Hard S (h(Z_S)=1): pick a minterm M of h with M cap S empty. Track wires with g(Z_S)=0, U(g)={x in S : g(1_M + e_x)=1}. Union-find over S gives >= |S|-1 merges (OR gates with g(Z_S)=0, |U(g)|>=2). The NOT is never a merge (N(Z_S)=0 and N(1_M+e_x)=0). For x not in S a tracked wire has g(1_M+e_x)=0 (1_M+e_x <= Z_S, both in {h=1}). No transversal T needed.
messages.P_scheme_conflicts: hard-hard (both P): a shared merge needs M_a cap S_b and M_b cap S_a both nonempty. easy-hard: NOT excluded (every minterm meets an easy set), whereas the Q=S cup T scheme does exclude easy-hard. So neither scheme alone closes charge_hard; untested idea: choose P or Q per hard set (Q when crossing with another hard set is empty, P otherwise).

messages.re: WARNING: most enumerated 'NOT read' circuits have a dead NOT; evidence for Lemma R / zero double merges is ~10x thinner than reported
finding: ov951.build only requires that SOME LATER GATE reads the NOT, not that the NOT lies in an output cone. Most circuits it returns are a monotone circuit plus dead gates (NOT -> junk gate read by nobody).
Measured on restr951.py's exact sample (5 systems, base+2/base+3, 15 per cell): 975 circuits, 887 have the NOT in no output cone. Only 88 are real tests of Lemma R.
Same on bigger systems: Pasch [(0,1,2),(0,3,4),(1,3,5),(2,4,5)] base+2: 2648 of 2700 dead-NOT; base+3: 2962 of 3000. Random n=6 5-set system base+2: 1324 of 1350.

So exh951's 586,352 base+2 circuits and the merge951b samples were very likely mostly dead-NOT too (not re-measured). The base+1 UNSAT results are NOT affected (they hold under the weaker 'read by a later gate' condition, so they are stronger).
messages.fake_R_violations: With dead NOTs allowed, Lemma R as written fails: Pasch, size 11 (base+3), h=x0, M={0}, gates [not x0; x3|x4; x3&w7; x0|w7; x1|x2; x1|x5; w8|w11; x0|w10; x2|x4; x5|w14; x5&w6], outs [13,9,12,15]: removed - sum_hit(|S|-1) = 1 < 2. The NOT feeds only the last gate, which nobody reads. So R (and 'NOT read => size >= base+2') MUST be stated with 'the NOT lies in the cone of some output'. Not a counterexample to 951.

messages.mechanism: absorption junk: w11 = x2 & (x2|x3) equals x2 and feeds the unhit output (1,2); it keeps the hit set's internal gate x2|x3 live after x_M=1. Each junk gate can keep a whole internal subtree of a hit set live.
messages.plus_0_form_also_false: agents/R_counterexample.py: n=8, S=(0,1,2,3,4,5), T=(5,6,7), 12 gates = base+5, h=x0, M={0}; junk gate (x1|..|x5)&x6 feeds o_T. Correct on all 256 inputs, NOT in cone of o_T, removed=4 < Σ_hit=5. So even 'removed >= Σ_hit(|S|-1)' fails; no bound on removed alone can work, since junk in the unhit part can keep hit-set gates live at 1 or 2 gates per subtree.
messages.not_a_951_counterexample: Both circuits have size >= base. Only the intermediate lemma breaks.
messages.repair_R2: Count junk-kept gates too. With x_M=1 fixed, for each UNHIT set S run the cone-restricted union-find with zero point Z_S and test points 1_M+e_u (this is coord's P scheme with one common M). R2: #gates that are a merge for no unhit set >= Σ_hit(|S|-1). R2 plus 'no gate is a merge for two unhit sets' plus '>= |S|-1 merges per unhit set' gives size >= base. On the two R-violators above: slack2 = 3 and 5, no unhit double merge.
